title: **Moving a profile package needs its removal first** — `replace()` rejects a retained profile mapping that moved to another directory or link target with `ResolutionRestartRequired`; removing the package and installing it again maps the new...

attrs.text: **Moving a profile package needs its removal first** — `replace()` rejects a retained profile mapping that moved to another directory or link target with `ResolutionRestartRequired`; removing the package and installing it again maps the new directory. A linked root may point to another directory once its profile mapping was removed. Node keeps the real path of every link it resolved through; once a link points elsewhere, or its name is installed again as a directory, a native lookup that selects a file below its previous target, for an importer outside it, selects the same file below the current one when that exists, including an explicit absolute path into the previous target. Installation mappings and local overrides still require a restart.

attrs.text: Every symbolic link below the profile's `node_modules` widens the comparison scope. Linking a package that the process entry point, located through the real path of a bin link, imports statically, such as `dsh-app-boot`, Cordis or the Loader from a dsh checkout, brings host modules into scope; their changes stay pending, and Plugin Manager reports `restart-required` for later operations until the process restarts. Linked dsh packages that Loader entries import are replaced like other plugins.

A replaced profile row passes the recomposition's preflight, but a row outside the profile composition, such as a preset row or an entry added through `ctx.loader.create()`, restarts with replaced code without a check. title: Only the reachability of a Git target's host is checked before the installed copy is removed, and only through Git: a host that only pnpm's own proxy settings reach is refused as unreachable. A target whose commit is missing, that needs cre...

attrs.text: Only the reachability of a Git target's host is checked before the installed copy is removed, and only through Git: a host that only pnpm's own proxy settings reach is refused as unreachable. A target whose commit is missing, that needs credentials pnpm lacks, declares no bundle, rejects the running DSH, or installs another package or version costs a stop and a reinstallation. The reinstallation uses the saved spec, from which the user information of an http(s) URL was removed, so a private repository needs a Git credential helper or the SSH form. A copy the SSH fallback saved for an HTTPS URL with a port loses the port, so its origin no longer matches the index's HTTPS spec and its updates are refused.

title: The Git transport probe keeps the parent console on Windows, so an SSH host-key or passphrase prompt can appear in the launching terminal until `gitTransportTimeoutMs`. On POSIX a host missing from `known_hosts` fails the SSH probe, so inst...

attrs.text: The Git transport probe keeps the parent console on Windows, so an SSH host-key or passphrase prompt can appear in the launching terminal until `gitTransportTimeoutMs`. On POSIX a host missing from `known_hosts` fails the SSH probe, so installation stays on HTTPS until the host key is accepted once, for example with `ssh -T git@<host>`. A credential-helper dialog or ssh-agent confirmation, such as a Touch ID or `ssh-add -c` dialog, that takes longer than the deadline counts as a failed probe, and an HTTPS probe that times out lets a reachable SSH form be saved to the profile. A private repository waits up to twice `gitTransportTimeoutMs` before pnpm starts. The SSH form always uses the `git` user and SSH's default port; other SSH endpoints need a `url.<base>.insteadOf` rule. When both probes fail, the diagnostic is pnpm's HTTPS failure; the SSH probe's reason is not reported.

title: **Whole-document reads** — the Host downloads and keeps each index up to `maxBytes` and builds its text index in memory; a synthetic index of 20,000 plugins took about 0.8 s of build time and 130 MiB of heap. Parsing runs in a Worker, but r...

attrs.text: **Whole-document reads** — the Host downloads and keeps each index up to `maxBytes` and builds its text index in memory; a synthetic index of 20,000 plugins took about 0.8 s of build time and 130 MiB of heap. Parsing runs in a Worker, but receiving the validated index still blocks the Host event loop while the clone is deserialized: about 35 ms for a synthetic 7.6 MiB index of 20,000 plugins and about 190 ms for 38 MiB and 100,000 plugins. Larger indexes need a server-side query protocol.
